newsitem.title: DUBAI: Arab Monetary Fund sets up credit rating agency.
newsitem.headline: Arab Monetary Fund sets up credit rating agency.

text.p: The Arab Monetary Fund said on Saturday it had joined forces with the European credit rating agency IBCA and the World Bank's International Finance Corp to set up a rating agency for companies across the Arab world.

Faris Bin Garadi, director of the Arab Monetary Fund's (AMF) economic and technical department, told a banking meeting in Abu Dhabi that the new Arab rating agency had also set up a subsidiary in Tunis and was working on other regional units.
He did not say when the main rating agency had been founded or where it was based.

"We are glad to inform you that the (Arab rating) company has set up a subsidiary company in Tunis...in November 1996 and has completed needed measures to set up a second company in Egypt," Garadi told the meeting.
"(The Egyptian) company is expected to start offering its services in the first quarter of next year," he said.
The "mother ratings company" formed by the AMF, IBCA and the International Finance Corp sets up the local rating firms in partnership with local companies.
Arab companies are rarely rated by major world institutions like Standard & Poors and Moody's, but some are assessed by a Cyprus-based agency.

The Abu Dhabi-based AMF -- the Arab world's premier financial institution -- was set up by 20 Arab governments in 1977 to lay the foundations for Arab economic integration and promote Arab economic development.
It provides eligible member countries with soft loans to assist financing balance of payments deficits in support of economic adjustment programmes.

The AMF has said the ratings agency would operate on a commercial basis and would not provide unsolicited ratings. The new company would also help standardise ratings across the Arab world and encourage companies to be rated as a service to their investors and clients.
Garadi said the Arab ratings agency was currently working on feasibility studies to set up three other subsidiaries in the Middle East.
